summary: Sporting News' Vinnie Iyer ranks all 32 NFL teams heading into Week 11 of the 2023 season, after a Week 10 that featured five walk-off field goals and several upsets. The Eagles stay No. 1, while the Lions and 49ers climb and the Texans leapfrog the Bengals and Bills. The Jets and Patriots slide, and the Panthers rank last. Each entry gives a team's record, prior ranking and a short assessment of its quarterbacks, coaches, offense and defense.
one_line: Sporting News' Week 11 2023 NFL power rankings put the Eagles first, lift the Lions, 49ers and Texans, and leave the Panthers last.
key_facts: The Philadelphia Eagles (8-1) stay at No. 1 after a Week 10 bye; their next four games are at the Chiefs (a Super Bowl 57 rematch), vs. the Bills, vs. the 49ers and at the Cowboys.
The Kansas City Chiefs (7-2) rise from 3 to 2 and regain the AFC's top seed after the Ravens lost.
The Detroit Lions (7-2) move from 5 to 3 and are called the second-best team in the NFC; the article says Dan Campbell is coach of the year.
The San Francisco 49ers (6-3) jump from 8 to 4 after a surprise offensive get-well game in Jacksonville led by Brock Purdy, even without Christian McCaffrey scoring.
The Baltimore Ravens (7-3) fall from 2 to 5 after a loss to the Browns in which Lamar Jackson made big mistakes; they face the Bengals on a short week.
The Houston Texans (5-4) rise from 16 to 13, ahead of the Bengals (5-4, down from 7) and Bills (5-5, down from 12); the Texans are led by C.J. Stroud and rookie coach DeMeco Ryans.
The Buffalo Bills fell into a trap game at home against the Broncos, losing because of more mistakes from Josh Allen.
The Las Vegas Raiders (5-5) jump from 22 to 16, having won two straight for interim coach Antonio Pierce.
The Minnesota Vikings (6-4) are 12th with Josh Dobbs at quarterback and look for a sixth straight win in Week 11 vs. Denver, after 0-3 and 1-4 starts.
The New Orleans Saints (5-5) are unsure at quarterback after Derek Carr further hurt his right shoulder and needed a concussion check; Jameis Winston provided a spark in a loss at Minnesota.
The New York Jets (4-5) fall from 18 to 21 after consecutive losses to the Chargers and Raiders, with Zach Wilson capping the offense until Aaron Rodgers can return.
The New England Patriots (2-8) fall from 28 to 30 after losing in Germany to the Colts, who won an ugly run-heavy game.
The Arizona Cardinals (2-8) rise from 32 to 29 with Kyler Murray and James Conner back.
The Carolina Panthers (1-8) are ranked 32nd, with Bryce Young unable to unlock a limited passing game.
